blocks.text: Imagine you are exploring a maze. How do you decide which paths to explore first? Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS) are two fundamental algorithms that help us traverse such networks efficiently.

blocks.markdown: In this lesson, we will delve into two essential graph traversal algorithms: Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS). These algorithms allow us to explore nodes and edges in a graph systematically.

blocks.title: Graph Traversal
blocks.text: Graph traversal refers to the process of visiting all the nodes in a graph in a systematic manner.

blocks.markdown: Both BFS and DFS are used to explore graphs, but they differ in their approach. BFS explores neighbors level by level, while DFS explores as far as possible along one branch before backtracking.

blocks.title: BFS and DFS Structures
blocks.text: BFS uses a queue to keep track of nodes to visit next, ensuring nodes are explored in layers. DFS uses a stack, often implemented via recursion, to explore as deep as possible before backtracking.

blocks.caption: Pseudocode for Breadth-First Search (BFS)

blocks.title: BFS Example
blocks.prompt: Perform BFS on the graph starting from vertex A.

steps.text: 1. Start at vertex A, mark it visited, and enqueue it.
2. Dequeue A, visit its neighbors B and C, mark them visited, and enqueue them.
3. Dequeue B, visit its neighbor D, mark D visited, and enqueue it.
4. Dequeue C, visit its neighbor E, mark E visited, and enqueue it.
5. Dequeue D and E, which have no unvisited neighbors.

blocks.answer: The BFS traversal order is A, B, C, D, E.

blocks.caption: Pseudocode for Depth-First Search (DFS)

blocks.title: DFS Example
blocks.prompt: Perform DFS on the graph starting from vertex A.

steps.text: 1. Start at vertex A, mark it visited.
2. Move to an unvisited neighbor, say B, mark it visited.
3. From B, move to an unvisited neighbor, say D, mark it visited.
4. D has no unvisited neighbors, backtrack to B.
5. Backtrack to A, visit another unvisited neighbor, say C, mark it visited.
6. From C, move to an unvisited neighbor, say E, mark it visited.

blocks.answer: The DFS traversal order is A, B, D, C, E.

blocks.title: Graph Type
blocks.text: These algorithms assume the graph is connected. If the graph is disconnected, additional steps are required to ensure all nodes are visited.

blocks.markdown: BFS is particularly useful for finding the shortest path in an unweighted graph, as it explores all nodes at the present 'depth' before moving on to nodes at the next depth level.

points: BFS and DFS are fundamental graph traversal algorithms.
BFS uses a queue and explores nodes level by level.
DFS uses a stack (or recursion) and explores nodes deeply before backtracking.
